sections.html:
Selling in Fitchburg comes down to three paths: hire an agent, go it alone, or deal with a cash purchaser who accepts whatever shape the property is in. Your deadline and the state of the house usually settle the question.

  • Agent listing: fits a clean, well-kept home, provided you can live with open houses and wait for a buyer's loan to come together.
  • For sale by owner: pricing, calls, negotiation and forms all land on your desk.
  • Cash buyer: a match for worn-out houses, tenant headaches, estates and fixed move dates, because there is rarely a repair list to argue over or a lender to wait on.

Renters fill much of Fitchburg. Just 47.6 percent of homes have their owner living inside, which means landlords and heirs of tenant-occupied houses make up a large share of sellers.

Fitchburg borders Madison on the south in Dane County, and its population keeps climbing. Citywide middle values are only a yardstick, so your own house may price higher or lower.

Owners still paying a mortgage spend a median of $2,384 monthly, and the average commute is 18.9 minutes. Quick drives into Madison are worth pointing out to buyers.

Building Inspection is the city office behind every permit for house work. You apply through its OpenGov portal. Inspectors measure one- and two-family homes against the 2021 International Building Code, the 2017 National Electrical Code and the 2016 Uniform Dwelling Code. A lender or buyer may want proof that past repairs had permits.

Think about what you changed while you owned the place. An unpermitted basement, furnace swap or deck is best brought to the city before a buyer discovers it. Phone 608-270-4240 or visit 5520 Lacy Road. Fixing a gap now beats scrambling once a contract is running.

For a permit that was opened and never closed, ask what inspections remain, then file the final sign-off with your sale papers. Cash buyers frequently accept a house along with its history. The disclosure form still expects honest answers.

Fitchburg wants short-term rentals to hold a city license, with each license year running July 1 through June 30. The city's application page charges $150 and asks for insurance proof, covering the property and liability, along with the county's hotel, motel or tourist rooming house license from Public Health Madison and Dane County.

If guests stay at your house, find out from the city whether the license can go to the new owner and cancel bookings after closing. Landlords with long-term tenants should read the lease, note when it ends and what notice the tenant is owed, and set a closing date around that.

Selling a property with one to four dwelling units triggers Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709. You owe the buyer a finished real estate condition report no later than 10 days after you accept the contract. Deliver it late and the buyer may withdraw in writing within two business days after the 10 days end, with deposits returned.

Each known defect goes on the form, line by line. A court-appointed personal representative, trustee or conservator who never lived there is released from the duty, as are transfers exempt from the state fee.

  • Complete every line. "Not aware of a problem" is a fine answer if it is true.
  • Attach any written engineer, surveyor or pest operator report that supports an entry.
  • Use the form the statute prescribes and update it if something changes before closing.

The seller bears the state transfer fee. Section 77.22 fixes it at 30 cents for each $100 of value, payable to the register of deeds as the deed comes in.

Records for Fitchburg land sit with the Dane County Register of Deeds. A deed there needs both parties named, a legal description, the tax-bill parcel number and the grantor's notarized signature. Photocopies are refused. Attach the electronic transfer return receipt, pay $30 for the document, and mail everything to PO Box 1438, Madison, WI 53701-1438 if you are not delivering it in person.

Certain transfers pay no fee. Section 77.25 excuses passage by will or descent and parent-to-child gifts for nominal or no value, with the reason written on the deed. The county treasurer can supply your tax balance so the closing agent can divide the year's bill with the buyer.

Once the buyer signs, the same chores follow, whether a bank or a cash buyer funds the deal.

  • Send the condition report before day 10.
  • Settle any open permit with Building Inspection, or disclose it.
  • File the electronic transfer return and hold on to the receipt.
  • Sign the deed before a notary and have the county register of deeds record it.
  • Pay off a mortgage and your share of taxes from the proceeds.

With cash there is no appraisal or loan underwriting, so title work and your own readiness set the pace. A listing piles showings, an inspection and loan approval onto the same list. Plan your move around whichever schedule applies.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html:
A tidy folder saves days later. Collect the items below before the first offer, since each one answers a question that a buyer, title agent or the register of deeds is likely to raise.

  • The latest property tax bill, which carries the parcel number the deed must show.
  • Permit records and receipts for any recent furnace, deck, basement or similar project.
  • The lease and tenant contact details, if anyone rents the house.
  • Your mortgage lender's name and loan number so a payoff figure can be requested.
  • Any engineer, surveyor or pest operator reports you hold.

Cash buyers lean on the same paperwork, though they generally ask fewer follow-up questions. If a document is missing, the city offices named above are the places to call, and the sooner you ask the less it can delay a closing.

A leased house passes to the buyer with its lease, so share a copy early. Buyers who want it vacant must agree a move-out date with the tenant, and that talk belongs in your schedule.

Closing speed depends on the buyer. Cash lets them choose a date that matches your move. Someone borrowing must wait for appraisal and final loan approval, so leave extra room.

One more habit helps in either case. Keep every email and signed page together in one place, and note the day each deadline starts, such as the day you accepted the contract. Counting from that day tells you exactly when the condition report is due and when a late delivery would let the buyer withdraw.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Fitchburg house sell?
faqs.a: Speed follows the buyer. Cash can close on a date you pick, whereas a listing waits on showings, an offer, an inspection and loan approval. The condition report is owed within 10 days of acceptance either way.

faqs.q: Must I have permit paperwork before selling in Fitchburg?
faqs.a: Nothing forces it to close, yet buyers and lenders ask. Ring Building Inspection at 608-270-4240 to learn whether your earlier work has a permit or an open one.

faqs.q: Who covers the Fitchburg transfer fee?
faqs.a: The seller. It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, and the Dane County Register of Deeds takes payment at recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell with tenants living in the Fitchburg house?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease and its notice terms. A buyer wanting a vacant house has to work out a move-out date with the tenant.

faqs.q: Which office records a Fitchburg deed?
faqs.a: The Dane County Register of Deeds, which takes the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and a $30 recording fee.
